_exec_summary.SummaryText:
This is an executive summary of the policies, procedures, and activities for compliance with the EPA's Accidental Release Prevention Requirements - Risk Management Program pursuant to Title 40 Part 68 of the Code of Federal Regulations (40 CFR 68) for the Clean Energy  East Valley Development (EVD) facility.

The accidental release prevention and emergency response policies at the stationary source [40 CFR 68.155(a)]:
EVD is strongly committed to employee, public, and environmental safety. This commitment is demonstrated by the resources invested in accident prevention, such as training personnel and considering safety in the design, installation, operation, and maintenance of our processes. Our policy is to implement reasonable controls to prevent foreseeable releases of regulated substances. The facility implements a Process Safety Management/Risk Management Plan Program in addition to other safety policies. This program includes governance of Employee Participation, Process Safety Information, Training, and other PSM element as well as details on the sites emergency planning and coordination with local responders.EVD is considered a non-responding facility for releases of the RMP-listed chemicals, so the site utilizes an Emergency Action Plan (EAP) which contains a map with evacuation routes, muster points and emergency equipment; a list of emergency phone numbers, and procedures for situations such as fires, chemical spills, and severe weather.

The stationary source and regulated substances handled [40 CFR 68.155(b)]:
The EVD RNG facility, located at 2694 E 750 S, Declo, ID, is designed to convert waste materials (such as manure) into a usable energy source, thereby reducing net greenhouse gas emissions.

Operated by Clean Energy, the facility includes an anaerobic digester, hydrogen sulfide (H?S) removal system, gas upgrading units, a compressor, storage systems, and various support infrastructure. The RNG process specifically focuses on separating component

s from the digester gas to purify methane for Renewable Natural Gas production.

The EVD facility handles biogas, which contains RMP-regulated substance Methane. This biogas is flammable and poses an asphyxiation hazard due to oxygen displacement. Methane, comprising approximately 70% of the biogas, is a colorless, odorless, and highly flammable gas. The quantity of biogas in the digester process exceeds the RMP threshold.

The general accidental release prevention program and chemical-specific prevention steps [40 CFR 68.155(c)]:
EVD is not required to implement the Program Level 3 prevention program requirements under the RMP regulations because they are eligible for RMP Program Level 1.

However, EVD is required to comply with the requirements for preventing or minimizing the consequences of catastrophic releases of flammable or explosive chemicals codified under the Process Safety Management (PSM) regulations (29 CFR 1910.119). The required elements of the PSM program relevant to general accidental release prevention are listed below:
?	Employee Participation
?	Process Safety Information
?	Process Hazard Analysis
?	Operating Procedures
?	Contractors
?	Pre-startup Safety Review
?	Mechanical Integrity
?	Hot Work Permit
?	Management of Change
?	Incident Investigation
?	Emergency Planning and Response
?	Compliance Audits
?	Trade Secrets

EVD has a program in place to comply with these items and their specific requirements.

The five-year accident history [40 CFR 68.155(d)]:
Clean Energy EVD facility is a new facility and has had no accidents meeting the definition in 40 CFR 68.42 in the past five years.

The emergency response program [40 CFR 68.155(e)]:
As a non-responding site, EVD has developed a written emergency action plan (EAP) that includes activation of the local emergency notification system and calling 911 from a safe location, and directing an evacuation, including exit route assignments. All employees are trained to assist other employees in a safe and

orderly evacuation. Should the scope of any incident exceed the capability of staff, such as a large flammable gas release, fire, or explosion at the facility, the employee discovering the emergency shall follow the protocol provided in the EAP to notify facility personnel, isolate the covered process if safe to do so, evacuate the facility and perform headcount at the designated muster point, and contact emergency responders. Emergency exit routes are through any available gate for this outdoor location and muster points. The facility is a non-responding facility and relies on the Raft River Rural Fire District when necessary to respond to RMP chemical releases.

Planned changes to improve safety [40 CFR 68.155(f)]:
EVD is continually improving and implementing its PSM/RMP program and safety systems. There is a process in place for the management team to review all potential process changes, including recommendations following process hazard analysis and compliance audits.  

EVD has completed this report to provide the public with information about our activities at this facility. We believe that, due to the many controls instituted to maintain a safe operation and our commitment to continuous improvement, an incident affecting our employees, or the surrounding area is unlikely to occur.
